title: Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Akiva
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, end of chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.6.8.2): an incident in which Rabbi Akiva made a feast for his son Shimon, and over each jug he said, “Good wine,” etc. The incident is cited in [Shabbat 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.67b.15), but his son’s name is not mentioned there.

His precious son died in his lifetime, in [Semachot, chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Semachot.8.13): when Rabbi Shimon, Rabbi Akiva’s son, was ill, Rabbi Akiva did not suspend his academy’s teaching; and when Shimon died, his father eulogized him and said: “I know that he is destined for the world to come, for he brought merit to the many.”[^1]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi names Shimon and gives wine jars. The linked Bavli is on 67b, gives cups and leaves the son unnamed. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3443&lang=en) places the toast at Shimon’s wedding. The linked Semachot has Rabbi Akiva keep teaching during Shimon’s illness and eulogize him afterward.
